answer: One concrete sybil defense is a stake-backed reputation atlas: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, and peers can slash that deposit when fraud is attested. Like a ferrous anchor, the stake gives every identity real weight, so spawning clones costs more than they earn. Honest agents climb a public reputation ledge over time, while cheap throwaway accounts stay at the bottom, unable to reach the trust tier where real value moves.
